tasks.short: Book training around shifts, rooms, equipment and instructor availability at our three sites.

today.trigger: A course is requested, new starters need training, or a mandatory certificate approaches expiry.
steps: Check Studytube for enrolments, training needs and certificate expiry dates.
Ask site managers about shift coverage and agency workers who need places.
Compare instructor, room and equipment availability using Outlook and local booking records.
Agree a date, register participants in Studytube and send invitations.
Update bookings and chase responses when attendance or availability changes.
drudgery: Exchanging emails to find a workable slot.
Checking the same booking constraints after every change.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: shift coverage and incomplete agency-worker records probably cause more delay than finding an empty classroom.

lenses.faster: A scheduling service checks availability and constraints together, removing spreadsheet comparisons and most booking emails.
lenses.autonomous: A new enrolment or certificate-expiry threshold starts scheduling automatically. Standard sessions are booked within approved rules; staffing conflicts go to the site manager.
lenses.ambitious: Give every starter a week-one training plan and reserve refresher places before certificates expire, including agency workers.
lenses.joy: Remove invitation chasing and repeated calendar checks. Spend the time helping managers release people for training and improving attendance.
lenses.options: Show several feasible schedules with travel, shift coverage, instructor cost and expiry risk for each.
lenses.altitude: Own the scheduling rules, capacity and exception process across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
reach: Site planning team: forecasts of training-related staffing demand.
Agency coordinators: allocation of flex workers to approved training sessions.

tasks.human_edge: Managers judge operational coverage and unusual attendance needs; qualified instructors determine safe class sizes and equipment requirements.
tasks.pattern_why: Dates, capacities, prerequisites and availability are structured constraints with checkable results. Build a rules-based scheduler; a language model is unnecessary for booking decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An approved training request, a new-starter record or a certificate entering its agreed renewal window.
steps: Load eligible participants, certificate dates, approved shift-release windows and training requirements.
Find slots that satisfy room, equipment, instructor, capacity and travel constraints.
Book a standard session if all constraints and spending limits are satisfied; otherwise present alternatives to the responsible manager.
Write the approved enrolments and invitations through verified integrations, or prepare an import where direct writes are unavailable.
Monitor changes, prevent duplicate bookings and route conflicts or failed writes to L&D.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers approve shift-release windows and L&D approves scheduling rules in advance. Exceptions, spending above the limit and changes outside those windows require approval before booking.
data_needed: Employee and agency-worker identifiers with permitted contact details.
Certificate expiry dates, prerequisites and course capacities.
Actual shift rosters and manager-approved release windows.
Instructor availability, qualifications and cancellation terms.
Room and equipment availability at each site.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint scheduling register recording constraint versions, approvals, booking identifiers, changes and integration failures.

evidence.claim: Outlook Scheduling Assistant supports availability checks for people and configured room resources; it does not establish warehouse shift coverage.
Rules-based scheduling can combine capacities, prerequisites and release windows when reliable structured data is available.
The 75% human-time saving and threefold completion speed are planning estimates, not measured results at Noordhaven.

risks: An empty calendar can be mistaken for permission to leave a warehouse shift.
Missing agency-worker records can leave flex workers outside mandatory training.
Studytube and roster integration permissions may limit automatic booking.
Paid training time, rest periods and travel must follow the applicable CAO and working-time rules.
Calendar and personnel access must be limited under AVG/GDPR; fixed instructor availability can still dominate elapsed time.
research_questions: Can each site supply current shift rosters and explicit training-release windows, including for agency workers?
Do our Studytube and Outlook configurations support reliable enrolment writes, resource bookings and change notifications?
In a pilot, how many bookings satisfy all rules without intervention, and does attendance remain at least as good?

tasks.short: Track training spending and explain the budget to HR and Finance.

today.trigger: Monthly reporting, a budget review or a request to justify a training purchase.
steps: Collect AFAS training expenses, supplier invoices and known commitments.
Match costs to courses, sites and participants using Studytube and Excel.
Resolve missing cost codes, duplicate entries and invoices covering several activities.
Compare actual spending and commitments with the approved budget.
Write explanations and review the report with HR and Finance.
systems: AFAS Profit general ledger and accounts payable
drudgery: Matching invoice descriptions to course names.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: inconsistent cost coding, unrecorded commitments and reconciliation to Finance's reporting period.

lenses.faster: A reconciled cost model produces the tables and variance flags automatically. AI drafts explanations from verified figures and supporting records.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh updates a draft training-cost view and opens exceptions for missing codes or unmatched commitments.
lenses.ambitious: Compare cost per completed course and per starter who becomes productive and stays 90 days, while keeping claims about training effects appropriately cautious.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet rebuilding and invoice-description searches. Keep the discussions about which training deserves funding.
lenses.options: Compare budget scenarios for onboarding volumes, renewal demand and internal versus external delivery.
lenses.altitude: Design the cost definitions and decision rules that make training investment visible and comparable across sites.
reach: FP&A Analyst: training demand and spending forecasts.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: agreed learning-cost measures.

tasks.human_edge: L&D and Finance decide what counts as training cost, whether spending is justified and what conclusions the evidence supports.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations and reconciliation produce the financial facts. A bounded language-model step turns those facts into a draft explanation that a person checks.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly extract completes successfully or the monthly reporting period is ready for review.
steps: Load AFAS expenses, the approved budget, recorded commitments and Studytube completion data.
Apply Finance-approved mappings, reconcile totals and flag incomplete or inconsistent records.
Calculate actuals, commitments, forecast spending and variances using deterministic formulas.
Draft explanations with references to the underlying figures and mark unsupported causes as unknown.
Have L&D and the Controller resolve exceptions and approve the report before publication.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the expenditure explanation and the Controller approves reconciliation and accounting treatment. The workflow cannot approve invoices, change ledger entries or release payments.
data_needed: Ledger lines, invoice references, cost centres and reporting periods.
Approved budgets and course-to-cost mappings.
Purchase commitments, cancellations and expected invoice dates.
Finance-approved treatment of VAT, accruals and internal trainer time.
Course enrolments and completions, using aggregate data where possible.
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted SharePoint monthly training-budget archive, including source refresh dates, reconciliation results, mapping versions and report approvals.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports refreshed data models and reports; Noordhaven's stated nightly AFAS extract supplies an existing reporting starting point.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI; user-supplied company system description

evidence.claim: A language model can draft variance commentary from supplied figures, but the figures and causal explanations need separate checks.
The 70% human-time saving and 2.5-fold completion speed depend on clean mappings and recorded commitments and have not been measured.

risks: Invoices alone understate future spending when commitments and accruals are missing.
Uncontrolled mappings can double-count shared invoices or misallocate costs between sites.
Generated commentary can invent reasons for a variance.
Training and retention correlations can be mistaken for causal effects.
A nightly refresh can produce a complete-looking report before month-close corrections are available.
research_questions: What proportion of training costs and commitments can be mapped reliably to a course, site and reporting period?
Which cost definitions and reconciliation tolerances will the Controller approve?
Does a two-cycle pilot reduce preparation time while matching the approved financial totals and preserving explanation quality?

tasks.short: Build a fair route from warehouse and office roles into future management positions.

today.trigger: Succession planning identifies a gap, a manager requests development support or HR reviews internal progression.
steps: Discuss future leadership requirements with HR Business Partners and site leaders.
Review existing development opportunities and barriers for shift and office employees.
Define learning goals, eligibility and a fair nomination or application process.
Design workshops, mentoring and supervised stretch assignments.
Agree release time and budget, run the programme and review participant feedback.
drudgery: Starting programme outlines and facilitator materials from scratch.
Repeating adaptations for different sites and shifts.
Combining feedback into usable programme revisions.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: agreeing leadership expectations, obtaining mentors and making development accessible alongside shift work.

lenses.faster: AI drafts programme outlines, practice cases and facilitator materials from approved leadership requirements. L&D spends less time preparing documents.
lenses.autonomous: Approved enrolments can trigger learning assignments and reminders. Decisions about potential, admission and promotion stay with accountable people.
lenses.ambitious: Offer a visible development route from picker or driver through team leader to management, with equivalent access for office employees and different shifts.
lenses.joy: Remove slide production and repeated material adaptation. Keep mentoring, difficult development conversations and watching people grow.
lenses.options: Compare mentoring, cohort learning and stretch-assignment routes, with different costs, release-time needs and support levels.
lenses.altitude: Own a fair leadership-development system and test whether it prepares people for real management responsibilities.
reach: HR Business Partner: programme design supporting succession planning.
Recruiter: clearer internal progression routes and management readiness requirements.
Site managers: structured mentoring and supervised development assignments.

tasks.human_edge: People establish trust, recognise context and judge readiness through observed work. Participants need honest feedback and meaningful opportunities, not an automated label.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can prepare learning designs, scenarios and alternatives. Leadership expectations, fair access, mentoring and individual development decisions require human leadership.

in_practice.trigger: HR approves a leadership-development brief addressing a defined succession or capability need.
steps: Agree leadership behaviours, entry criteria, shift-access requirements and measures of programme success.
Give AI approved role descriptions and anonymised workplace scenarios to draft several programme options.
Review the options with HR Business Partners, site leaders and prospective participants; select the design and confirm mentors.
Produce reviewed learning materials and publish the approved pathway in Studytube and SharePoint.
Run mentoring and supervised practice, then use aggregate feedback to revise the programme.
in_practice.human_gate: HR and L&D approve the programme and materials; accountable managers make participant and progression decisions. Involve the OR where the design introduces arrangements subject to consultation or consent.
systems: AFAS Profit for authorised administrative records
data_needed: Approved leadership expectations and role descriptions.
Transparent eligibility and application or nomination rules.
Mentor capacity and manager-approved release time.
Language, accessibility and shift requirements.
Anonymised practice cases and aggregate programme feedback.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint programme register with approved criteria, material versions, design decisions and evaluation results; individual development records remain in their approved HR location.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft learning outlines, role-play cases and alternative development plans from a supplied brief.
Mentoring, fair participant selection and readiness judgments still need human observation and responsibility.
The 35% human-time saving and 1.4-fold completion speed are untested estimates for programme design and administration, not faster leadership development.

risks: Manager nominations can favour visible office employees or particular shifts.
Generic materials may miss the responsibilities of managing a Dutch logistics operation.
Stretch assignments can become unpaid extra work or unsafe delegation without clear boundaries and supervision.
Using AI to rank employees or influence promotion could bring the system into EU AI Act high-risk employment uses; assess intended use before any such extension.
Individual assessments need an AVG/GDPR basis, access controls and retention limits; consult the OR on relevant personnel assessment arrangements.
research_questions: Which leadership gaps require a programme, and what observed behaviours would demonstrate readiness?
Can all sites and shifts provide paid release time, mentors and fair access to development?
Do reviewed AI drafts reduce design effort, and does the resulting programme improve readiness without widening participation gaps?

tasks.short: Teach practical ways to reduce waste, energy use and avoidable work in our operations.

today.trigger: An operational improvement, environmental target, audit finding or changed site procedure requires training.
steps: Ask operations and safety or environmental owners which behaviours need to change.
Collect approved site procedures and examples of current waste or inefficiency.
Create training materials and practical exercises for the affected roles.
Arrange delivery across sites, shifts and relevant agency workers.
Check understanding and review operational results with the process owner.
systems: Power BI where suitable operational data exists
drudgery: Turning long procedures into short lessons.
Reworking the same lesson for each site and language.
Writing quizzes and combining course feedback.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: obtaining accurate site-specific procedures and arranging practical instruction during busy shifts.

lenses.faster: AI turns approved procedures into draft short lessons, quizzes and shift briefings, reducing repeated writing and formatting.
lenses.autonomous: A published procedure revision creates a training-impact review and draft updates. Approved lessons can then be assigned to the relevant groups automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Build short lessons around recurring errors in waste sorting, packaging and energy use, and test whether the relevant behaviour improves.
lenses.joy: Remove document conversion and repetitive quiz writing. Keep hands-on demonstrations and conversations with workers about what makes the procedure difficult.
lenses.options: Compare a toolbox talk, visual job aid, short digital lesson and practical exercise for each behaviour.
lenses.altitude: Design a repeatable process that connects approved operational changes to training and checks whether people use the new practice.
reach: Operations improvement team: training support for process changes.
Safety and environmental owners: communication of approved procedures.
HR Administrator: onboarding assignments for site-specific environmental training.

tasks.human_edge: Site experts validate technical instructions and instructors observe practical performance. Workers explain why a procedure succeeds or fails under real operating conditions.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can draft and adapt learning content from approved procedures. Technical validation, practical teaching and attribution of operational improvements remain human work.

in_practice.trigger: A process owner approves a procedure change or requests training for a specific environmental or efficiency problem.
steps: Collect the approved procedure, affected roles and sites, target behaviour and baseline measure.
Draft lesson formats, quizzes and language variants with references to the source procedure.
Have the process owner and a suitable language reviewer check instructions and translations.
Pilot the approved materials on one relevant shift, adjust them and assign the final training through Studytube.
Compare practical observations and operational measures before and after delivery, accounting for changes in workload.
in_practice.human_gate: The operational and safety or environmental owner approves every technical instruction before publication. Practical competence and any regulated certification require the appropriate human assessment.
systems: Excel or an authorised operational Power BI dataset
data_needed: Current, approved procedures and their owners.
Site-specific waste streams, equipment and operating constraints.
Target roles, shifts, languages and literacy needs.
Approved examples and permission to use workplace photographs.
Relevant baseline measures, workload denominators and observation criteria.
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint procedure-linked training register, recording source versions, technical and language approvals, pilot feedback and links to Studytube completion reports.

evidence.claim: Language models can turn supplied procedures into draft learning materials and questions, subject to technical review.
Studytube manages courses, enrolments and completions in Noordhaven's stated setup; automatic procedure-change integration still needs verification.
The 40% human-time saving and 1.5-fold completion speed are untested estimates; no reduction in waste or energy use is assumed.

risks: Incorrect waste-handling, equipment or food-safety instructions can cause harm or noncompliance.
Translations can change technical meaning, and digital lessons may be unsuitable for some learners.
Course completion can be mistaken for demonstrated practical competence.
Operational improvements can reflect volume, equipment or process changes rather than training.
Training assignments must cover agency workers and fit paid training arrangements under the applicable CAO.
research_questions: Which specific behaviours cause measurable waste or inefficiency, and can training reasonably change them?
Are approved procedures current for each site, and who can validate technical content and translations?
Does a shift-level pilot reduce preparation time and improve observed practice when workload and process changes are considered?

role.altitude: Become the owner of learning pathways, training capacity and evidence of practical readiness across all three sites, with routine scheduling and reporting handled by governed workflows.
reach: HR Administrator: training assignments and onboarding completion checks.
HR Business Partner: leadership-development design and fair internal progression routes.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: learning data definitions and training-outcome reporting.
Controller and FP&A Analyst: training cost analysis and demand forecasts.
Operations and agency coordinators: training capacity planning and support for approved process changes.
role.ceiling_note: These four tasks total 219.8 hours per FTE per year, or 439.6 hours across two FTE. The proposed savings release about 258 hours annually, roughly EUR 17,535 of capacity at EUR 68/hour, before setup and maintenance; this is not a cash saving or an estimate for the entire role. Instructor availability, shift release, practical assessment, mentoring and human accountability limit further automation.
skills_to_grow: Learning data quality, financial reconciliation and Power BI interpretation.
Instructional design for shift workers, varied literacy levels and multiple languages.
Evaluation that separates completion, competence and operational outcomes.
Fair development pathways and consultation with the OR.
AVG/GDPR controls and EU AI Act assessment of proposed employment-related AI uses.
Technical review of AI drafts and management of workflow exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Give every employee and relevant agency worker a clear route to safe, productive work, with week-one learning, timely certificate renewals and accessible development opportunities. Work with managers to measure practical readiness and connect learning to the share of hires who become productive and remain after 90 days, while accounting for other causes of retention.
